h1: The 6 Best Over-the-Range Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six over-the-range microwaves compared on vent CFM, capacity, width, and venting type, from 1.4 to 1.9 cubic feet.
summary: The GE 1.9 cu. ft. is the best over-the-range microwave, with 1000 cooking watts, a 400 CFM fan and convertible venting. The BLACK+DECKER matches its size and airflow. The 30 inch and 24 inch GE models fit standard and compact ranges, and the recirculating GE suits kitchens without an outside duct.
intro: An over-the-range microwave is two appliances bolted together: a cooking box and a stove-top exhaust fan. Most shoppers only evaluate the first. The fan rating, the width of your cutout and whether the unit can vent outdoors or only recirculate decide whether it actually works above your range, and a wrong guess means a return and a drilled cabinet.

We ranked six models from their listings on capacity, wattage, vent CFM, width and venting method. All six sit in the $200 to $500 bucket, so the ranking is about fit and features rather than price. Measure your opening before you read any further.

products.name: GE Over the Range Microwave Oven with 1.9 cu. ft. Capacity
products.verdict: Big chamber, 400 CFM, and venting you can convert.
products.description:
This GE has a 1.9 cu. ft. chamber, 1000 cooking watts, 10 power levels and a 400 CFM vent fan with convertible venting. It sits in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It wins because convertible venting lets you choose between ducting outside and recirculating, which suits most existing kitchens without surprises. The BLACK+DECKER matches its capacity and airflow, but its listing is less clear on venting. A large chamber and a strong fan together cover the two jobs this appliance has.

Buy it for a family kitchen with a busy cooktop. Measure the cutout before ordering, since 1.9 cu. ft. is a large unit that will not fit a narrow opening. The listing does not describe extras beyond the basics, so check the manual for installation clearances.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Over the Range Microwave Oven (1.9 Cu.Ft)
products.verdict: Matches the GE on capacity and airflow.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER lists 1.9 cu. ft., 1000W and a 400 CFM vent. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket, with the same headline numbers as the GE above.

Second place is decided by one missing line. The listing does not mention convertible venting, so you cannot be sure how it handles ducting. Otherwise it is a strong match, with a roomy interior and the same fan rating. If the venting works for your kitchen, this is an equal alternative from a different brand.

Buy it if you want the large interior and strong airflow from a second maker. Skip it if you need to confirm convertible venting before buying. Ask the seller or read the manual to learn how it exhausts, and check the large footprint against your cabinet space.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a roomy interior and strong airflow.
products.skipIf: You need to confirm convertible venting.

products.name: GE 30" Over-the-Range Microwave
products.verdict: A 30 inch fit with a 300 CFM hood vent and LED lighting.
products.description:
The GE 30 inch model is built for a standard 30 inch range space, with 1.6 cu. ft., 1000 watts, a 300 CFM hood vent and LED lighting for the cooktop.

It ranks third because the fan is weaker than the 400 CFM units and the chamber is smaller than the 1.9 cu. ft. models. What it adds is a dependable fit for the most common cutout width and cooktop lighting that makes it easier to see what you are cooking. For a typical kitchen, that practicality often matters more than raw airflow.

Buy it for a standard 30 inch range where light to moderate cooking is the norm. Skip it if you fry or sear heavily and want the strongest fan. A 300 CFM vent may leave smoke lingering after a high-heat meal.

products.name: GE 24" Over-the-Range Microwave
products.verdict: A 24 inch width for compact ranges.
products.description:
The GE 24 inch model is designed for a compact range, with 1.4 cu. ft., 1000 watts, a 300 CFM hood vent and LED lighting.

Fourth place follows from its smallest capacity here. A 1.4 cu. ft. chamber is fine for plates and mugs but limits larger dishes. It is the one to choose for a compact kitchen where the wider models simply will not fit, and for that job nothing else in this list works.

Buy it for an apartment or small kitchen with a 24 inch range. Skip it if you need a big chamber, since the 1.9 cu. ft. models offer nearly half again as much space. Measure the cutout twice, because a width error is the main reason these appliances come back.

products.name: Midea Over the Range Microwave Oven
products.description:
The Midea lists 1.7 cu. ft. and 1000W. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket, and sits between the largest and smallest chambers in this group.

It lands fifth because the listing gives no vent CFM and no venting details, which makes it hard to judge as a range hood. For an appliance that is half exhaust fan, that omission is a real weakness. The cooking specs look healthy, but the ventilation story is a blank.

Buy it if you want a mid-size interior and plan to confirm the vent specifications elsewhere. Skip it if airflow over the stove matters to you, since the GE and BLACK+DECKER models document their fans. Contact the seller to find out the CFM and whether it vents outside before you order.

products.name: GE Over-the-Range Microwave Oven with Recirculating Venting
products.verdict: A recirculating 1.8 cu. ft. unit with a removable turntable.
products.description:
This GE offers a 1.8 cu. ft. chamber, 900W, a 12.8 inch removable turntable and 10 power levels, with recirculating venting.

It ranks last because 900W is lower than the 1000W units. Recirculating venting also filters air back into the room instead of removing it, which is less effective at clearing steam and smoke. Its strength is where it works: any kitchen without an outside duct, where the vented models cannot be installed.

Buy it if you have no exterior vent path above your range. Skip it if you want the highest wattage or true outside venting. A removable turntable makes cleaning simpler, and a 1.8 cu. ft. interior is roomy enough for large plates, so the real tradeoff is airflow quality.

whatMatters.detail: Vent CFM is how much air the hood fan moves, and higher figures clear smoke and steam faster. It matters over a busy cooktop. Find it in the title or bullets. Listings here run from 300 to 400 CFM, and the Midea lists none.

Width is the size of the opening the microwave must fit. Common range widths are 24 and 30 inches. A mismatch means a return. Measure your cutout and compare it with the listing. The GE 24 inch and GE 30 inch models state their widths, while the others are sized for standard spaces.

Venting method describes where the exhaust goes. Convertible venting lets you duct outside or recirculate, while recirculating filters air back into the room. Check your kitchen for a duct path before choosing. The first GE is convertible, and the last GE recirculates only.

Capacity, in cubic feet, decides which dishes fit. This list runs from 1.4 to 1.9 cu. ft. Check the number and the turntable diameter. The largest chambers suit family cooking, while the 1.4 cu. ft. GE suits compact kitchens.

Wattage affects how fast food heats. The models here range from 900W to 1000W. Look for the figure in the title. Most list 1000W, while the recirculating GE lists 900W, which means slightly slower cooking for the same job.

faq.q: Do I need an outside vent?
faq.a: Not always. The convertible GE and the recirculating GE work without one, though recirculating filters air back into the room instead of removing steam and smoke outdoors.
Skipping the width. The microwave has to match the cutout above your range. A GE 30 inch will not fit a 24 inch space, and the GE 24 inch will look undersized in a 30 inch one.
If you cook often, yes, because the BLACK+DECKER and first GE move more air than the 300 CFM models. For occasional cooking, a 300 CFM GE may be enough.

It mounts to a wall bracket and the cabinet above. Follow the manual for each model, such as the Midea or GE. Hire a professional if you are unsure, since a heavy unit overhead needs secure fastening.

faq.q: How do I maintain the vent?
faq.a: Clean or replace the grease filter regularly, as the manual describes. Recirculating models, like the last GE, also have a charcoal filter that needs replacing, so check the schedule.

faq.q: Can I use it above a gas range?
faq.a: Check the manual for clearance requirements before installing. A microwave above a gas range needs enough distance to the burners, and the requirement varies by model, so confirm it for the GE or BLACK+DECKER you choose.

finalTake: For most kitchens the first GE, with 1.9 cu. ft., 1000 watts and a 400 CFM convertible fan, is the over-the-range microwave to buy. The BLACK+DECKER is a close alternative if the venting checks out. Pick the 30 inch or 24 inch GE by your range width, and the recirculating GE only when no duct exists. Measure first, always.
